title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: reduce inference unit cost by providing safe, production-ready defaults and tooling for batching, KV-prefix caching, and quantization profiles. This PR implements a conservative autotune default layer that picks batching/window policies and cache hot-prefix heuristics per-model-family, adds first-class quantization profile metadata for common families (LLAMA2, MPT, GPT2-style), and surfaces unit economics calculations in the console and CLI tooling. The goals are: (1) reduce average tokens-per-second unit cost for common request patterns, (2) avoid SLO regressions by keeping latency tail protections and model fallbacks, and (3) give platform teams visibility into the cost/quality tradeoffs via unit-econ reports. Changes: - runtime: new default batching policy config (autotune.safe_defaults) with max_batch, pref_min_size, latency_target_ms thresholds - runtime: KV cache: prefix-based hot-cache heuristic and TTL defaults; integrates with existing prefix cache metrics - model-registry: added quant_profiles.json schema and sample profiles for llama2-13b, mpt-7b, redwood-13b-q4 - control-plane: API to suggest autoscaling/batch parameters for Dedicated pools based on workload traces - console: unit-econ report panel (per-route SKU cost, effective tokens/sec, recommended quant/profile, estimated monthly savings) - cli: redwood ctl unit-econ generate --route <route> --period 7d - tests: end-to-end perf harness runs against the perf-canary scenarios and added unit tests for config merge logic Rollout plan: staged feature-flagged rollout (autotune.safe_defaults off by default). Beta for internal customers for 2 weeks, then enable gradual ramp for low-risk routes. Checklist: - [x] runtime defaults implemented - [x] quant profiles schema and samples - [x] console + CLI UI for unit-econ - [x] perf regression tests (no tail latency regressions observed in canary) - [x] doc updates and changelog entries - [x] telemetry hooked for decision tracking Notes: this PR intentionally errs on conservative defaults (smaller max_batch for latency-sensitive models, aggressive fallback to unquantized models for routes with quality tags). Related: ENG-1214 (autotune defaults), ENG-1305 (unit economics tooling).

merge_summary: Squashed 9 commits into main. Autotune safe defaults, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling added. No regressions observed in canary. Feature flagged by default.
release_notes: Conservative autotune defaults for batching and KV caching, quantization profile metadata in model registry, and unit-economics tooling (console + CLI). Feature-flagged rollout; intended to reduce unit cost while preserving latency SLOs.
testing_notes: Perf canary runs included interactive (single-turn) and batched workloads. Measured up to 18% median cost savings for batchy routes and <3% median latency increase. Tail p99 latency was within SLO for all tested models. E2E harness and unit tests added.
rollback_plan: Feature-flag off immediately if regressions detected; control-plane suggestion endpoint can be disabled via feature gate. Revert PR if critical regressions. Alerting configured on p99 latency and error-rate spikes.
